title: Choose a project with less searching
summary: Compare the proposed picker states. Each example is a static HTML recreation with its own feedback field.
recommendation: Use a searchable list with a clear selected row. Keep feedback beside each proposed state.
scope: This example reviews layout and messages. It does not implement a project picker or claim current product behavior.

sections.title: Review the proposed states
sections.summary: Review the layout and messages at full size. These are proposed states, not screenshots of an existing product.

items.title: Recent projects stay visible
items.body: Show recent projects before the first search. Keep the selected project clear without relying on color alone.
criteria: Keyboard users can move between projects.
The selected row includes a text label.

details.title: Interaction
details.body: Keep focus in the search field while filtering. Announce the result count without moving focus.

items.title: Explain an empty search
items.body: Keep the query visible. Offer a clear way to try another search.

previewFile.label: Proposed empty search - static HTML recreation

criteria: Clear search returns to recent projects.

items.title: Show that results are loading
items.body: Keep the search field available. Announce that the project list is loading.

previewFile.label: Proposed loading state - static HTML recreation

items.title: Give a failed request a next step
items.body: Explain that the request failed. Preserve the search and let the user retry.

previewFile.label: Proposed failed request - static HTML recreation

criteria: The page does not display a failed request as an empty result.

sections.title: Resolve before implementation
sections.summary: Record the decision that changes which projects the picker can show.

items.title: Which projects can the user see?
items.body: Use the existing permission owner. Establish whether unavailable projects are hidden or shown with an explanation.

details.title: Evidence needed
details.body: Read the current permission contract before choosing a display rule. This example does not propose changing access.
